sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with Ghost Gloveworts.

- As a red-eye Spirit Ash, this knight will remain at the spot where they are summoned and pursue any encroaching enemies aggressively. Quite fitting for the masterless knight known as the Rabid Stray.
- Like other, hostile Bloodhound Knights, Floh is quite fragile and reliant on being able to chain staggers and Blood Loss to burst down foes without being killed. Due to this, Floh is best used by a build that can keep attention away from them and that can take advantage of the additional Blood Loss build-up to more easily cause the status themself.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- The name Floh seems to stem from the name of the prehistoric Floian period, a trait shared with Bloodhound Knight Darriwil, who in turn seems to be named for the Darriwilian period.
 - The only other enemy with this etymological origin are the three named Crucible Knights: Ordovis, Siluria, Devonia.
 - Crucible Knight Floh was the boss of the Erdtree-Gazing Evergaol in early development. This location was renamed Forlorn Hound Evergaol and now contains Bloodhound Knight Darriwil.

- The "Rabid Stray" seeking a lord of true caliber may reference the ancient Greek philosopher —known for his futile search for a wise (honest) man and later of , the most powerful man in the world.
 - Diogenes was nicknamed a “barking dog” for his and austere lifestyle. Some accounts claim he died from a dog bite.
 - *"At the approach of so many people, Diogenes sat up a little and fixed his eyes on Alexander. When the king greeted him and asked if there was anything he wanted, Diogenes replied, 'Yes, that you should stand a little out of my sun'. It is said that Alexander was so impressed by this—and by the arrogance and grandeur of spirit of a man who could treat him with such disdain—that he said to his courtiers, who were laughing and joking about the philosopher as they walked away, 'But I'll tell you this: if I were not Alexander, I would be Diogenes!'"* — Plutarch, Alexander, XIV

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ashen Remains**, also referred to as **Spirit Ashes**, are items in Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree that allow players to summon spirits to assist in combat.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
There are two main types of Ashen Remains. **Ashes** are used to summon basic allies while **renowned ashes** call forth mighty heroes from the past. Each Spirit Ash can be upgraded to a maximum of +10 by Roderika, Spirit Tuner by trading her Glovewort flowers. Spirit ashes may be improved further with Revered Spirit Ashes; however, their bonus is only applied to the Realm of Shadow. Once the first Revered Spirit Ash has been collected, their Shadow Realm Blessing may be strengthened at any Site of Grace.
- Grave Glovewort is used to improve standard Ashes
- Ghost Glovewort is used to improve special Renowned Ashes
- Revered Spirit Ash is used to improve the Shadow Realm Blessing

sections.heading: How to use Spirit Ashes
sections.markdown:
To summon spirits, players must possess the Spirit Calling Bell and be within the radius of a Rebirth Monument. The desired ash can then be activated directly from the inventory. Most spirit ashes require either FP or HP to summon, and only one ash can be summoned at a time.

Rebirth Monuments are small obelisks scattered throughout the Lands Between. They are required to summon spirit ashes, and their presence is indicated on the screen with a specific icon. These monuments are commonly found near boss arenas or areas with dense clusters of enemies.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Black Knife Catacombs** is a dungeon in Elden Ring.

It is found by heading east from the Church of Vows and taking the south path in the north-south split road. From there, follow the road until another north-east split happens and head north again before the cliffside splits east and follow it.

The entrance to the catacombs is guarded by a Mausoleum Knight.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A catacomb in the north-eastern area of Liurnia, inhabited by Necromancers and Skeletons. The catacombs are said to contain a knifeprint which hides the truth of the conspiracy of the Night of Black Knives.

Skeletons in this dungeon cannot be killed normally after being defeated unless using special weaknesses of Those Who Live in Death. Instead, nearby Commoners wielding special staves have to be killed to finished them off normally.

The entrance to the main boss arena can be found just after the Site of Grace at the entrance. Head left to find a split in the route, with a Stonesword Key-locked room to the left that holds 2 Skeletons and the Rosus' Axe.

To continue, head forward instead of to the left and run into a large room with 3 guillotines.

sections.heading: Main boss route
sections.markdown:
Run through the guillotine to a ladder and climb down. Straight ahead is the dungeon lever, guarded by 2 Giant Crabs that pop up from the back and the front as you approach.

Return to the entrance and head through the now unlocked door to arrive at the boss, a Cemetery Shade who is accompanied by 2 sword-wielding Skeletons and 2 bow-wielding Skeletons. Since this can be a very overwhelming fight it is recommended to bring a Spirit Ash to distract at least some of the foes, or otherwise bring a strong anti-undead attack such as the skill Sacred Blade to deal with the mobs.

sections.heading: Secondary boss route
sections.markdown:
After the second or third guillotine blade has fallen down in the large room they can be stepped onto and ridden to a ledge above. Following through the door leads to more regular enemies as well as a corridor that seemingly ends with a small hole to the right to drop down to the lever below. If one instead attacks the wall straight ahead another fog wall for a boss will be revealed, along with the summon sign for D, Hunter of the Dead should he be alive.

Since the Black Knife Assassin within is a very agile foe capable of making lunges across the rather small arena, it is advisable to summon D or a Spirit Ash to help keep the assassin's attention on someone else and get a safe moment to heal.

sections.markdown: Blade of Calling** is a melee armament found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Loot:** Forbidden Lands
Hidden within a room that you can only reach during the elevator ride that leads down to the Forbidden Lands grace, alongside the Official's Attire.

Jump from the southwestern part of the elevator to a doorway just above the bottom floor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- While its Faith-scaling is technically the strongest its Dexterity-scaling is effectively almost equal to it because the dagger's Physical base Attack Power is higher than its Holy base Attack Power.
 - An equal split between Dexterity and Faith will give the most Attack Power (AP), though a pure Dexterity build or a pure Faith build will get only about 5% less AP.
 - Since the skill scales with weapon upgrade level and Faith but not Dexterity or Strength, it can be beneficial to lean into the pure Faith build, or even a 45/45 or 30/60 Dex/Fth split.
 - A pure Faith (80) build gives 1138 Holy Attack Power, 13% more Attack Power on the skill than hybrid Dexterity/Faith (45/45) build's 1010 Holy Attack Power and 5.5% more Attack Power than the skill of a Faith-leaning Dexterity/Faith (30/60) build's 1079 Holy Attack Power.
- Unfortunately generally outclassed by the Black Knife. While this weapon is 0.5 units lighter, has better scaling, and its skill deals more outright damage at a lower FP cost, the Black Knife will always have more AP due to higher base Attack Power, is attainable much earlier in the game, and the skill is often more damaging due to part of its damage being percentage-based.
- Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Erdsteel Dagger, and Fire Knight's Shortsword.
 - This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2 due to hitting twice.

- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base Attack Power while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base Attack Power: red for Fire Attack Power, yellow for Lightning Attack Power, orange for Holy Attack Power, and cyan for Magic Attack Power.

sections.markdown: Blackguard Big Boggart** is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Boggart is an ex-convict who was called to the Lands Between by the Guidance of Grace. At some point in the past he was imprisoned in the same gaol as the Dung Eater, and saw first hand the ways he defiles and kills people.

The Tarnished first encounters him in Liurnia of the Lakes, where they confront him over the theft of a necklace belonging to Rya. Despite his foreboding first impression, Boggart gives the Tarnished the opportunity to buy back the necklace, and offers to sell them some cooked crawfish.

Boggart then journeys to Altus Plateau, setting up camp beside a river outside the capital, where he catches and cooks crabs. Here, he warns the Tarnished about the Dung Eater. Should the Tarnished ignore his warnings and release the killer from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, Boggart will become his latest victim.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Boilprawn Shack)
 - Head north-west from the Site of Grace to find Rya the Scout inside a gazebo and talk to her.
 - Move to north-west again from here to find Blackguard Big Boggart at the Boilprawn Shack and talk to him: select **Give me the necklace** and then **Deal** to be able to buy Rya's Necklace from him for 1000 Runes.
 - After purchasing the item, he'll start selling an infinite supply of Boiled Prawns. Purchase at least one to progress his questline: you'll receive the "Spread Out" gesture and, in turn, Boggart's summon sign will appear at the Ruin-Strewn Precipice Overlook to aid you against Magma Wyrm Makar.
1. Altus Plateau
 - After resting at a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau, Boggart will move to the outer moat along the northern wall of Leyndell, Royal Capital in the Capital Outskirts (due west from the Capital Rampart Site of Grace).
 - You may now purchase an infinite supply of Boiled Crabs.
 - Exhaust Boggart's dialogue about Dung Eater. After freeing Dung Eater from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning Grounds, Boggart will have some additional dialogue.
1. Altus Plateau
 - After hearing Boggart's final piece of dialogue about Dung Eater, warning you that Dung Eater is lurking nearby, reload the area to find Boggart bound to a chair. Speak to him to trigger an invasion from Dung Eater.
 - Defeat Dung Eater and return to Boggart, who is now dead. Loot his equipment, as well as the Seedbed Curse.

sections.markdown: The **Bloodstained Dagger** is a Dagger in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- 2% drop rate from Fierce Demi-Humans aka Demi-Human Chiefs.
 - One can point asleep next to the bridge west of the South of the Lookout Tower Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Strong Strength- and Arcane-scaling.
 - Surpasses all daggers except the rather unusual Wakizashi for raw damage on a Heavy affinity and has the highest Strength-scaling of them all, just short of an S-rating.
 - Second or third strongest dagger on the Occult affinity, though it will only slightly outmatch the Reduvia (only by 1 point) and the latter will have more Blood Loss build-up.
 - Pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.
 - Despite this its Heavy affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Storm Blade, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy).
- The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult).
 - While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage.
- The only dagger with a Strength focus on its Cold affinity instead of a Dexterity focus.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The was an unseen character mentioned in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The blind swordsman was an ancient nomadic warrior, clad in sturdy leather and blue fabrics symbolizing waters as brisk and fluid as the blade in his hand. According to legend, he received a curved sword patterned after rushing waters from a fairy, represented by the Dancer in Blue.

The ever-drifting hero traveled the Ainsel River to the Lake of Rot, where still waters grew stagnant with scarlet rot in the presence of a great scorpion. Blade in hand, he confronted the outer god of Rot with the fluidity akin to a dance—allowing his foe to strike, then exploiting the opening with a well-timed counterattack. The blind swordsman defeated the ancient god and sealed away its divine essence.

During the age of the Elden Ring, the Blind Swordsman encountered the young Demigod Malenia and became her mentor. Despite being born into the accursed rot, she gained wings of unparalleled strength. However, Malenia would eventually abandon her pride to meet General Radahn's measure during the Battle of Aeonia, producing in the Swamp of Aeonia.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Blind Swordsman invented the Guard Counter technique, the art of allowing one's opponent to strike to leave them vulnerable to a well-timed reply.
- The Prosthesis-Wearer Heirloom depicts the Blind Swordsman clasping left hands with Malenia; both figures wear prosthetic right arms.
- Wore the Blue Cloth Set, which is used by the Warrior starting origin. This armor set bears a striking resemblance to the Blue Dancer Charm fairy.
 - The blue color of the set symbolizes brisk waters, emphasizing flow, and stresses the need to remain ever drifting. As such, the Blind Swordsman may be related to the nomadic warriors who wear the Blue Cloth set.
- The hero's Flowing Curved Sword is housed within a Great Coffin in the Consecrated Snowfield.
- The Blue Dancer Charm and Shamshir are found among ancient ruins in Highroad Cave.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Blood Loss** is a status effect in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Blood Loss is usually caused by serrated, thorned, exremely sharp, or bloodstained weapons. Spells and items affiliated with the Lord of Blood also cause this status effect.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.markdown:
Deals a combination of flat and percentual damage when inflicted and humanoid or smaller enemies, and Tarnished, are slightly staggered. The flat damage is usually 100, but increases to 200 when done by Somber Smithing Stone-upgraded weapons with innate Blood Loss and Arcane-scaling or by regular Smithing Stone-upgraded weapons with innate Blood Loss and with the Blood-affinity. The percentual damage depends on the enemy: normal ones and Tarnished take 15% damage, bosses and enemies that directly accompany them take 10.5% damage, and the Lord of Blood takes 7.5% damage.

Additionally, the blood loss inflicted by Mohg's Nihil attack is unique and only inflicts percentual damage, roughly 33% damage on each of the first two pulses and about 66% on the final pulse. Using the Purifying Crystal Tear greatly reduces this damage to about 5% on the first two pulses and 10% on the final one.

Blood loss can also be inflicted on someone in the middle of invincibility frames, such as a roll, though this only causes the stun and not the damage.

sections.heading: Buffs related to Blood Loss
sections.markdown: There are certain equipment that gives the player buffs when blood loss has been inflicted in the general vicinity, they do not discriminate between what has been bled in order to activate, it can be friend, foe and even oneself and generally lasts for around 20 seconds since the last blood loss infliction.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Banished Knights** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Knights who, whether by misfortune or misdeed, were forced to abandon their homes. Most were sent to the fringes, forced to start anew with only despair for company. Many of them wear helms adorned with sculptures of dragons, although some cover their helms with deep red scarves to protect themselves from the biting winds of the fringes.

The Banished Knights wielded the power of the storm and practiced Dragon Communion. They are predominantly found in Stormveil Castle, Castle Sol, and Crumbling Farum Azula, often accompanied by Exile Soldiers. Spectral versions of these knights can be encountered at Castle Sol on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

Two notable Banished Knights are Oleg and Engvall, referred to as the Wings of the Storm. After their banishment, they were extended invitations by the Grace-Given Lord. While Oleg accepted this invitation and later earned Erdtree Burial, Engvall rejected it and instead chose to watch over a masterless castle, gaining reknown as a hero of the fringes.

Some of these knights are capable of using Dragon Communion Incantations, such as Dragonfire, while others utilize storm arts. Spectral versions of these knights can be found in Fringefolk Hero's Grave in the Stranded Graveyard within Limgrave.

These enemies can disappear and reappear. Some cannot be snuck up on, and will teleport behind the player, even when attacked from distance.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, is encountered within a secluded, starlit cavern somewhere along the underground Ainsel River, beyond the Lake of Rot. This area is accessed by entering the Transportation Coffin overlooking a chasm at the Grand Cloister. The elevator Astel blocks is the only path to the hidden Moonlight Altar, a necessary step for Ranni the Witch's questline.

- Defense: 114
- Stance: 120
- Deals Standard and Magic damage
- Cannot be Parried
- Vulnerable to a Critical Hit after being stance broken

sections.heading: Trivia

- The internal data Astel's boss arena includes spawn markers for an Ancestor Spirit and its spirit animals, suggesting the Grand Cloister boss was reassigned to Astel from a third Ancestor Spirit encounter.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Basilisks** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: Basilisks are amphibious creatures that haunt many regions of the Lands Between, favoring places tainted by Death. These squat, finned quadrupeds move in short hops and lash out with claws or sudden leaps, but their most significant threat is the black fog they exhale, which spreads Death Blight. The grotesque, bulbous eyes on their heads are a deception—the true eyes are small and set far back near the snout. These false eyes resemble the Prince of Death's, with similar pupils appearing in the tainted roots that wind through graveyards and catacombs.

- Ainsel River – in dark cave areas
- Ancient Ruins of Rauh – summoned by the Divine Beast Dancing Lion
- Auriza Hero's Grave
- Deeproot Depths – found in and around the Nameless Eternal City
- Lake of Rot – submerged in the scarlet rot
- Mt. Gelmir – along and to the north of the Seethewater River

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Resistant to most Status Effects
- Vulnerable to Fire and Slash damage
- Cannot be Parried
- Can be Stance-Broken, but cannot be Critical Attacked
- Affected by Beast-Repellent Torch and Beastlure Pot
- The Prince of Death—the soulless body of Godwyn the Golden—has finned forelimbs, much like a Basilisk.
- Basilisk statues in Scorpion River Catacombs inflict Death Blight via line of sight.
- In Elden Ring Nightreign, Basilisks populate the sewers of Noklateo, the Shrouded City.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Basilisks are a recurring enemy in the *Dark Souls* franchise, having appeared in all three games. Typically, Basilisks inflict Curse or petrify the player. Although these status conditions do not appear in *Elden Ring*, their Death Blight-inflicting clouds work similarly.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Bloody Fingers** are a covenant of invaders from Mohg the Lord of Blood's burgeoning Mohgwyn Dynasty. By his will, these bloodthirsty Tarnished hunt their own.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
This group of Tarnished is similar in practice to the Recusants of the Volcano Manor, in that Bloody Fingers seek out and kill other Tarnished throughout the Lands Between. However, they seem to differ in long-term goals as well as rites of induction. To become a Bloody Finger, one must be inducted via a process overseen by a White Mask, such as Varré. The first step is to prove their dedication to their Lord's cause by hunting fellow Tarnished, using fetishes made from Furled Fingers blackened with blood congestion, to invade their worlds as blood-red phantoms; these seem to have been chopped off rather unceremoniously. Killing one Host of Fingers, or attempting to do so at least three times, is enough to pass this step. Next, the inductee must stain a special cloth, the Lord of Blood's Favor, in the blood of a Tarnished's Finger Maiden. One need not necessarily kill a maiden, let alone their own maiden, to do so, as long as they can obtain the blood. With this done, it can be brought to the White Mask.

The initiate, now a formal Bloody Finger, is then given one last blessing: the Lord of Blood's own glistening blood, siphoned into the nail of their finger. This Bloody Finger's skin becomes sickly pale and loses feeling, although the nail aches with sweetest pain. The process is agonizing, but it gives the ability to invade other worlds as often as they like without the need for the consumable fingers. Over time, the inductee begins to fall to "cessblood", an infection-like condition that causes an onset of bloodlust and insanity, removing any inhibition that would prevent the Bloody Finger from killing their fellow Tarnished with a zealous devotion to Mohg.

The new Bloody Finger may also be given a Pureblood Knight's Medal, with the power as to gain an audience with Mohg himself, when the time is right; obtaining one sometimes requires the White Mask to go out of their way to obtain it.

There are those that hunt the Bloody Fingers in return, however: Yura is one such warrior seeking to put an end to their cessblood. The group has taken notice of this, however, and sent assassins after him.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Bayle the Dread** is an optional boss in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Enemy of the Dragonlord
sections.markdown: Bayle the Dread was a legendary black dragon who is said to be the ancestor of the drakes or lesser dragons. Long ago, Bayle betrayed the Ancient dragons and clashed with Dragonlord Placidusax. Their vicious battle ended in stalemate and left both dragons with grievous injuries and loss of body parts, with Bayle losing his two winged arms, his pair of wings on his back and his left leg, with the dreaded dragon fleeing to the Jagged Peak soon afterwards.

sections.heading: Dragon Communion
sections.markdown:
As punishment for his betrayal, Placidusax created the art of Dragon Communion, sending his followers to shepherd humanity into hunting Bayle and his descendants. As reward for felling the drakes, the dragon hunters consumed their hearts in order to gain their power. Bayle was pursued by Florissax, a servant of Placidusax who sought to recruit mortals in the hunt for Bayle.

Dragonslayer Igon, a particularly obsessive drake warrior, was one such mortal. Igon faced Bayle, but was left broken in both body and spirit by their battle.

sections.heading: Drake Warrior
sections.markdown:
Igon was stumbled upon by a Tarnished champion, and begged them to summon his spirit to face Bayle once more. Together, the pair succeed in slaying Bayle.

If Bayle's heart is eaten at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion, his willpower will one day consume the body and soul of the drake warrior.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.markdown: Bayle is weakest against piercing damage, Dragon Communion Grease, and Igon's Harpoons.

sections.heading: Phase One
sections.markdown: Bayle is stuck on the ground. He commands a unique power that combines fire and lightning damage.

sections.heading: Phase Two
sections.markdown: Bayle summons an extra set of wings made from red lightning. He is able to fly.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Two of Placidusax's lost heads can be found still clinging onto the upside of Bayle's neck.
- The ancient dragons who sided with Bayle against Placidusax wielded the branching red lightning.
- Drake Warrior Igon may be summoned inside the area if the player has received his Furled Finger.
- Igon and Florissax will reward the player after Bayle is defeated.
- Bayle is the only boss in the game who displays the text 'Legend Felled' when defeated who does not drop a Remembrance. Rather, he drops the Heart of Bayle, which functions similarly, with some differences.
 - The Heart of Bayle cannot be redeemed for an item by meeting with Finger Reader Enia. Rather, it must be redeemed at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion.
 - The Heart cannot be consumed to receive Runes, nor duplicated.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Bayle's name is a corruption of "bale," which refers to a destructive and evil force.
- Bayle's name and moniker "The Dread" may also be a reference to the dragon *Balerion*, *The Black* *Dread* from author and the base game's co-writer George R. R. Martin's fantasy novel series, *A Song of Ice and Fire*.

sections.heading: Effect

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Long ago, the abyssal serpent was a powerful snake in the Lands Between. It was separated from its light, although it is unclear by whom, when, or why. If it was not so already, it henceforth became a wicked entity.

Messmer, son of Queen Marika, was born cursed with the essence of the base serpent stirring within him. His mother's fear drove her to suppress its power, so she replaced his right eye with a golden Scarseal of Grace. Later, she trapped him within the Realm of Shadow on an endless crusade against those stripped of her Grace. The abyssal serpent slowly consumed Messmer's Kindling, but its influence was limited by his constant companions, the winged serpents.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Information regarding this character is limited.
- If the base serpent did not possess Messmer from birth, then it was placed there by Marika herself.
- It is unclear whether the shed snakeskin near the Bonny Village belonged to the base serpent.
 - The skin is adjacent to the O Mother statue, implying a connection to Messmer. However, its appearance more closely resembles the flayed snake found in the Temple of Eiglay than the attacks of Base Serpent Messmer.

sections.heading: Trivia

- Messmer refers to the Base Serpent as "光無き、深淵の蛇が" that can be translated as "the Lightless, Serpent of the Abyss", without the idea that it was "shorn of light" but rather that it had always been lightless (光無, Hikarina, lit. "Without light").
- Messmer unleashes the base serpent by divesting himself of his mother's light.
 - Marika's actions ironically led to the base serpent's unsealing.
- In the Japanese version, the "base serpent" is called 邪な蛇 (*"Wicked Snake" or "Evil Snake"*).
 - The English word "base" is used to express a deficiency in character or status (*ignoble, baseborn, base instincts*).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Beastmen** are a faction in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The beastmen were bestial humanoids who served the ancient dragons in ages past, wielding weapons clad in red lightning. They inhabited Crumbling Farum Azula, the ruined city in the sky, and were once granted five fingers of intelligence. Many were honored warriors of the Sun Realm, while others were chosen to guard the giant mausoleum of Dragonlord Placidusax.

The beastmen forged heavy yet balanced curved weapons from dull iron, and fired earthenware jars specifically to make shields. Despite their crude works, they possessed knowledge beyond human understanding.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.markdown: True to their name, Beastmen appear to be half-man, half-canid humanoids with sharp claws, furry tails, and large snouts full of sharp, bloodstained teeth. Their skin is covered with scraggly dark gray fur, with bare patches exposing raw flesh and even bones, most notably on their lipless, skull-like faces. Although most Beastmen dress in little more than ragged wrappings and loincloths, stronger warriors can be seen clad in iron armor and chainmail, and all Beastmen decorate their bodies with unalloyed gold jewelry, including bracelets, crowns, and necklaces adorned with precious stones. They can be found wielding curved swords, jar-shields, or sickle-like throwing blades. Grey-haired Beastmen wield Clawmark Seals, which they use to cast lightning incantations. Some beastmen wield weapons imbued with red lightning, which deal lightning damage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Bloodfiends** are enemies in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Long ago, a subjugated tribe was saved from the ravages of war when they encountered the Formless Mother, who transformed them into bloodfiends.

The bloodfiends make offerings of blood to the Formless Mother, sometimes even spilling their own blood in devotion. Their sacred spears are central to their rituals, serving as instruments of communion with the mother of truth, an outer god who desires a wound. From her wound, Sacred Bloody Flesh may fall—a raw, blood-soaked meat that never dries or rots, valued as a delicacy by the bloodfiends.

The bloodfiends cultivate Sanguine Amaryllis, blood-red flowers with meaty petals, grown in pools of blood. These flowers may reflect their admiration for the beauty of blood.

sections.markdown: Some of their weapons, sanctified through blood rituals, are capable of spraying stored blood when executing strong attacks.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Boc's mother** or **Mum** was an unseen character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Boc's mother was a highly skilled demi-human seamstress whose dedication to her craft left a lasting impact on her son. Her ability to create garments from scratch surpassed even the royal seamsters of the Erdtree capital. Among the sewing tools Boc inherited, her curved needle—shaped like a fang—stood out as a cherished symbol of her craft and the deep bond they shared. She taught him the art of tailoring, inspiring his deep desire to follow in her footsteps.

Though Boc struggled with his appearance, his mother was the only one who called him beautiful, giving him a sense of self-worth that he clung to throughout his life. Her memory drove him to perfect his skills, always striving to live up to the talent and kindness she embodied.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: Boc's mother was a demi-human with deft hands. Her compassionate voice was recorded by a Prattling Pate, which can be found in the Hermit Village on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Her unconditional affection for Boc was immortalized in the wistful Prattling Pate, which captured her tender words: *"You're beautiful."*
- Boc's mother was likely a member of nobility. She possessed specific knowledge of the royal seamsters, who repaired the clothes of the demigods.
- The lattice ornamentation featured on her sewing needle is identical to the stitching on the Mask of Confidence. Both designs are simplified version of the trellis of Radagon's Rune, and the seals on the Academy of Raya Lucaria gates and the Erdtree itself. The lattice design represents the threaded needlework both characters are known for.
 - Boc later trades in his mother's needle for the golden sewing needle once owned by Radagon of the Golden Order.
